text:
Cherie DeVaux's Golden Tempo won the Belmont Stakes after winning the Kentucky Derby(Image: Getty Images)

Golden Tempo clinched victory in the 158th Belmont Stakes to add to its Kentucky Derby crown for trainer Cherie DeVaux.

The $2 million New York Triple Crown finale featured a nine-horse field and marked the third straight year the Belmont Stakes has been held at Saratoga while Belmont Park undergoes modernized renovations. It is also the final time.

Confined by Saratoga's tight, sweeping turns, the Triple Crown’s grueling mile-and-a-half marathon was stripped down to a mile-and-a-quarter sprint for this year's event. Jockey Jose Ortiz has now commanded Golden Tempo in both of its Triple Crown wins after not participating in May's Preakness Stakes.

The victory served as another memorable chapter in the Triple Crown season after Golden Tempo stunned the horse racing world by winning the Kentucky Derby at 23-1 odds. The historic wins made DeVaux the first woman to achieve both wins.

However, Napoleon Solo won the Preakness Stakes after Golden Tempo did not run in the race as DeVaux chose to skip the middle jewel of the Triple Crown to give the horse extra rest. After clinching victory in the Belmont Stakes, DeVaux did not want to entertain the thought of a potential Triple Crown eluding her grasp.

“It’s not something I want to think about,” DeVaux said. “We made our decision and we won today, so we’re going to be happy about that.”

DeVaux jumped for joy as her horse began the race from Post Position 9, which was the outermost gate in the nine-horse field. Once the horses went four of five wide, Golden Tempo exploded from the pack and outdueled Commandment in the final stretch for the victory.

Jose Ortiz rode Golden Tempo to victory in the 158th Belmont Stakes(Image: Getty Images)

“Still trying to catch my breath,” DeVaux said when interviewed by FOX Sports after the race. “Golden Tempo is amazing. Jose is amazing... it’s just a lot of amazing feelings. I have to name a horse ‘amazing’ now.”

She added: “It’s so meaningful. A lot of family here. Saratoga has been wonderful, to have such a historic race here is like an appetizer for the meat. It’s so meaningful because the town gets to have this and celebrate it along with all of us.”

DeVaux is in fine company. The first woman ever to train a Belmont Stakes winner was Jena Antonucci in 2023, when Arcangelo won the 155th running of the race. The victory also made Antonucci the first woman to train a winner of any American Triple Crown race.

Pre-race attention centered on Renegade as the Arkansas Derby winner and Kentucky Derby runner-up. The horse also entered the race as the 2-1 morning-line favorite.

Chief Wallabee was also heavily favored at 3-1, while Golden Tempo successfully added another Triple Crown race to his growing resume after his historic success at Churchill Downs.
